### Kind

### Agent

### Size

Cargo.lock

### Spec
Spine: section 5, D-02, D-05, D-20, D-63, P14. Design: docs/design/03 sections 1, 2, 4, 10 and 11, work item A1 (design/03 A1); docs/design/10 sections 1 to 3; docs/design/11 sections 1, 2 and 4. Decision records: ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0006, ADR-0010, ADR-0022, ADR-0029. Requires: #1550 (the implementer must be able to write `architecture.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `**/AGENTS.md`) and #454 (a `workflow_dispatch` run of `verify.yml` on the head, for AC-4). The root `Cargo.toml` already declares `members = ["crates/*", "programs/*"]`, `exclude = ["bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf"]` and the workspace lints, so it does not change.

Re-specified by lead-core after ADR-0029 removed the harness and the `xtask` crate. The earlier attempt (pull request #438, branch `agent/2/a2`) was built with `xtask` as a workspace member and `cargo xtask verify` as its gate, and now conflicts with `main`. It is not continued: the implementer starts fresh on `issue/2` and may read #438 only as background.

Lead squad: core. The skeleton also creates empty crates whose paths other squads own. Each of those leads accepted the plan in a comment on this issue (team/01 section 2), and their changes are folded into R2, R3, R4, R7 and R9 below:
- security (`grdr-crypto`): accepted; the skeleton creates no `crates/grdr-wire/src/peer_auth*` (that module arrives with #375).
- adapters (`grdr-agents`, `grdr-hook`): accepted.
- endpoint (`grdr-store-local`, `grdr-sandbox-engine`, `grdr-daemon`, `grdr-engine`, `grdr`): accepted with `grdr-store-local` privileged.
- linux (`grdr-sensor-linux`, `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf`): accepted with the bpf crate's own lints, contents and build check.

Each squad fills its own crate in its own items.

#### Problem
`crates/` and `programs/` are empty, so Cargo refuses every gate command and no later item can add code. Every slice 0 item is blocked on the crates, their layer metadata and `architecture.toml`.

#### Non-goals
- No behaviour in any crate: each is an empty library, or a binary whose `main` returns success.
- No architecture lint (design/03 A2, #1580 and its sibling items), no new gate in `verify.yml`, no licence or supply-chain change, no new dependency (the bpf crate takes no `aya-ebpf`; its toolchain, target and dependencies are #406's).
- No change to `security/trust-core.paths` or design/02's D-63 list.
- `grdr-strings` and `grdr-messages` (squad interfaces, #449 and #1119), `grdr-broker` and `grdr-conformance` (#225), `grdr-run` and the other `grdr-sandbox-*`, and every crate whose `Requires` column in design/03 section 2 is not "Nothing".
- No `crates/grdr-wire/src/peer_auth*` (security squad, #375).
- `Cargo.toml` and `rust-toolchain.toml` do not change.

#### Behaviour
- R1. The workspace gains 21 members, each with `[lints] workspace = true` (except R4's two) and `license = "Apache-2.0"`: libraries `grdr-proto`, `grdr-schema`, `grdr-model`, `grdr-core`, `grdr-llm-proto`, `grdr-fastpath`, `grdr-ffi`, `grdr-wasm`, `grdr-fastpath-ffi`, `grdr-ports`, `grdr-ports-testkit`, `grdr-crypto`, `grdr-wire`, `grdr-sensor-linux`, `grdr-agents`, `grdr-store-local`, `grdr-sandbox-engine` under `crates/`; binaries `grdr-daemon`, `grdr-engine`, `grdr-hook`, `grdr` under `programs/`. `grdr-hook` has `src/main.rs` only (#376 adds its `src/lib.rs`).
- R2. `bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf` is a library crate outside the workspace (already in the root `exclude`, plus its own empty `[workspace]` table so Cargo does not walk up to an enclosing manifest), licensed `GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause` (ADR-0004). No crate depends on it, and it has no dependencies of its own (design/10 R2: the object is built separately and loaded). Its `src/lib.rs` starts with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause` and is `#![no_std]`. It has no `rust-toolchain.toml` and no `bpfel` target (#406). Its own `Cargo.lock` is committed.
- R3. Each crate declares `[package.metadata.grdr]` with `layer`, `privilege`, `surface` and `renders`, and its `AGENTS.md` header carries the same values plus `squad` and `trust core`, exactly as the table below. Layers 0 to 2 are `surface = "public"`, layers 3 and 4 `internal`.

  design/03 section 2 defines the four `privilege` values but assigns none per crate, so lead-core fixed them by one rule, read from design/03 sections 1 and 4 and design/11 sections 1 and 4 and the programs that run each library's code:
  - A program takes its process's privilege: `grdr-daemon` is `privileged` (root or LocalSystem in `protected`, the minimal core; design/11 "Security and privacy" lists it as privileged), `grdr-engine` is `sandboxed`, `grdr-hook` (agent session) and `grdr` (user surfaces) are `untrusted` (design/11 section 1).
  - A layer 3 library is `privileged` when design/03 section 1 or design/11 puts its code in the daemon or the kernel, otherwise `none`. `sandboxed` and `untrusted` describe a process, so only programs carry them.
  - A layer 0 to 2 library is `none`. It is a public crate that every host links (spine section 5; embedding hosts, the server, the engine), its checked arithmetic comes from its layer (R4), and ARCH-004 binds it through the privileged program's closure, not through its own value.

  | Crate | Kind | Layer | privilege | surface | renders | squad | trust core | Why this privilege |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `grdr-proto` | lib | 0 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-schema` | lib | 0 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-model` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-core` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | no (module `policy` is) | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-llm-proto` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-fastpath` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | yes | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-ffi` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | yes | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-wasm` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-fastpath-ffi` | lib | 1 | none | public | none | core | yes | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-ports` | lib | 2 | none | public | none | core | no (module `tenant` is) | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-ports-testkit` | lib | 2 | none | public | none | core | no | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-crypto` | lib | 2 | none | public | none | security | yes | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-wire` | lib | 2 | none | public | none | core | no (module `peer_auth` is, security squad) | layer 0 to 2 rule |
  | `grdr-sensor-linux` | lib | 3 | privileged | internal | none | linux | no | runs in the daemon, holds the BPF descriptors and writes the enforcement maps (design/03 section 1 actuators; design/10 Interfaces) |
  | `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf` | lib, not a member | 3 | privileged | internal | none | linux | yes | runs in the kernel |
  | `grdr-agents` | lib | 3 | none | internal | none | adapters | no | its translators parse content, so ARCH-004 keeps it out of the daemon; the engine and the CLI link it |
  | `grdr-store-local` | lib | 3 | privileged | internal | none | endpoint | no | the spool is daemon-owned (design/11 section 4); the engine's recorder also links it |
  | `grdr-sandbox-engine` | lib | 3 | privileged | internal | none | endpoint | yes | only the daemon calls it (design/03 section 2) |
  | `grdr-daemon` | bin | 4 | privileged | internal | none | endpoint | yes | program rule |
  | `grdr-engine` | bin | 4 | sandboxed | internal | none | endpoint | no | program rule |
  | `grdr-hook` | bin | 4 | untrusted | internal | agent | adapters | no | program rule |
  | `grdr` | bin | 4 | untrusted | internal | person | endpoint | no | program rule |

  `trust core` is `yes` when a glob in `security/trust-core.paths` covers the whole crate directory; a crate with only a trust-core module says `no` and names the module in its `AGENTS.md` invariants. `renders` is `person` for the CLI's human output and `agent` for the shim's block messages; every other crate returns `MessageRef`s and formats nothing (design/03 section 10, "Text").
- R4. `grdr-core` has the empty modules `analyze`, `session`, `policy`, `detect`, `discover` and `compile`. `grdr-fastpath` is `#![no_std]` with no dependencies. Every layer 0 to 2 crate and every crate R3 marks `privileged` (`grdr-sensor-linux`, `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf`, `grdr-store-local`, `grdr-sandbox-engine`, `grdr-daemon`) carries `#![deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects)]` at its crate root (ADR-0022). `grdr-ffi` and `grdr-fastpath-ffi` carry their own `[lints]` table, a copy of the root's workspace lints with `unsafe_code = "deny"` in place of `workspace = true`, and contain no `unsafe` yet. `grdr-sensor-linux` and `grdr-sandbox-engine` keep `workspace = true` until their first `unsafe` item, which moves them to that copy inside its own write set.
- R5. `architecture.toml` holds, as data: the layer of every crate of design/03 section 2, including those not yet created (marked `created = false`); the complete same-layer edge list of section 2 (layer 1's "every crate except `grdr-fastpath` and `grdr-fastpath-ffi` to `grdr-model`" may be one rule entry); the two decoders ARCH-004 admits; and the `tool` layer rule.
- R6. Every dependency edge between members is a lower-layer edge or a listed same-layer edge, and only edges a skeleton needs exist. Empty crates need none, so no member has a dependency.
- R7. Each of the 22 crates of R1 and R2 has an `AGENTS.md` with every heading of `docs/agents/templates/crate-AGENTS.md`, its header filled from R3's table, and its sections filled from design/03 sections 1 and 2 plus R9. A field with no content yet says "none yet" and names the item that fills it, never a path that does not exist.
- R8. Layer 0 and 1 crates build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (ARCH-003; the target is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`).
- R9. The `AGENTS.md` of each crate another squad owns states, as its owning lead asked on this issue:
  - `grdr-crypto`: trust core (security/trust-core.paths); the only crate that links cryptography (ARCH-006). First content #334, #336, #337.
  - `grdr-agents`: holds per-agent installers, managed-source probes and structural dialect translators; hook payloads are parsed here and never in `grdr-hook` (ARCH-004); event names, tool names, matchers and version ranges are manifest data (P14). Its edges come with #370.
  - `grdr-hook`: its closure links no `grdr-core`, `serde_json`, `regex`, `grdr-strings` or `grdr-messages` (ARCH-004, ARCH-024); it writes its output by hand; the shim answers within 2 s; on Windows Claude Code calls it for `PowerShell` as well as `Bash` (#1560).
  - `grdr-daemon`: the minimal core of design/03 section 1; its closure holds no content parser, only the generated protobuf codec (ARCH-004); it never depends on `grdr-core`; it reaches no network and binds no TCP listener (design/11 section 14); it exposes only `decide`, `local` and `provider`, each peer-checked (design/11 section 1); it is the only writer of every lane (R-08). First content #1536.
  - `grdr-engine`: the one session monitor and all parsing; it holds no keys, enforces nothing, verifies no signature, writes no lane and reaches no network (design/03 section 1); the daemon starts it over an inherited channel inside `grdr-sandbox-engine`'s profile (design/11 sections 1 and 2); it returns `MessageRef`s and formats no text.
  - `grdr`: it shows state and proposes changes, and mutates nothing without a grant (D-31); it reaches the daemon only over `local`; commands, flags and exit codes come from `interface/cli.toml`, and `main` returns the generated `ExitCode` (ARCH-023); `programs/grdr/**` is an interface path, judged by eval-ux and eval-a11y.
  - `grdr-sandbox-engine`: one launcher for all three systems, called only by the daemon; it returns the sandbox report the engine echoes in `Hello`, and a missing element sets `engine-sandbox-partial` (design/11 section 2); it is an OS adapter crate (R4's `unsafe` rule).
  - `grdr-store-local`: spool, SQLite local history and flight recorder; it is in the daemon's closure, so ARCH-004 binds it; a non-ALLOW receipt is fsynced before the reply (design/11 section 4); segment and offset arithmetic is checked. First content #428.
  - `grdr-sensor-linux`: design docs/design/10 sections 1 to 3; implements `SensorBackend` and `Actuator` (design/10 Interfaces) and only collects and enforces (D-20); decodes fixed-layout ring records only; never sets a provenance grade (the daemon stamps it); the probe never branches on distribution name or version (design/10 section 1); never takes a Cargo dependency on `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf` or on `grdr-core` or another content parser (ARCH-004); kernel enforcement needs S-12 and the D-63 review (D-19); R4's `unsafe` rule.
  - `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf`: trust core (`bpf/**`, D-63), design/10 sections 2 and 3; the object's licence string is `Dual BSD/GPL`; programs are written in Rust with aya-ebpf, and a program aya cannot express is written in C in its own directory of this crate; CI builds the signed `.o` the back end loads (ARCH-011); oracles are the kernel verifier on the design/10 section 14 matrix and the reference model of #107; kernel enforcement waits on S-12 and the D-62 review. First content #26.
- R10. `grdr-sensor-linux-bpf` is not a member, so `[lints] workspace = true` cannot resolve for it. It carries its own `[lints]` table, a copy of the root's workspace lints with `unsafe_code = "deny"` (aya-ebpf helper calls will need reasoned `unsafe`, as the OS adapter crates do), and contains no `unsafe` yet.

#### Mechanism (P14)
Layers, privileges, edges and admitted decoders are data in `architecture.toml` and `[package.metadata.grdr]`. The architecture lint (design/03 A2, #1580) reads them; this item adds no reader and writes no layer or privilege fact in code.

Data classes (P8): none, no field is read or written. Assurance effect (P1): none.

#### Failure modes
| Failure | Declared outcome | Visible as |
|---|---|---|
| A crate missing metadata, or with a value other than R3's table | AC-1 fails | the evaluator's diff of `cargo metadata` against R3's table |
| An edge that is not allowed | AC-2 fails now; ARCH-001 once A2 lands | `cargo metadata` graph |
| A crate fails to build on one system | AC-4 fails | the failing `verify.yml` job |
| An `AGENTS.md` header disagrees with R3 | AC-6 fails | the header line against R3's table |
| The bpf crate fails to build, format or lint, or gains a dependency | AC-7 fails | the `--manifest-path` command's exit code and `cargo metadata` output |
| A layer 0 to 2 or privileged crate root lacks the arithmetic lint | AC-8 fails | the path `git grep -L` prints |

### Plan
- [ ] 1. Create the 21 members and the bpf crate (`cargo new --lib` or `--bin`, `--vcs none`) - verify: `cargo build --workspace --locked`
- [ ] 2. Add `[package.metadata.grdr]` from R3's table, the lints of R4 and R10 and the `grdr-core` modules - verify: AC-1 and AC-8
- [ ] 3. Write `architecture.toml` - verify: AC-2, read against design/03 section 2
- [ ] 4. Fill each `AGENTS.md` from the template, R3 and R9 - verify: AC-6, then the four gates of `grdr-verify` (AC-3)
- [ ] 5. Layer 0 and 1 on wasm32 - verify: AC-5
- [ ] 6. The bpf crate's metadata, licence, SPDX line, lints and lockfile - verify: AC-7

### Acceptance criteria
```json
{"schema": "grdr.agents.acceptance.v1", "item": 2, "criteria": [
  {"id": "AC-1",
   "check": "cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 --no-deps",
   "expect": "exit 0; the workspace members are exactly the 21 packages of R1, and each carries metadata.grdr with layer, privilege, surface and renders equal to its row of R3's table",
   "oracle": "the crate table of docs/design/03 section 2 for layers, and R3's table (derived from design/03 sections 1 and 4 and design/11 sections 1 and 4 by R3's stated rule) for privilege, surface and renders, read against Cargo's own metadata"},
  {"id": "AC-2",
   "check": "cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1",
   "expect": "exit 0; every dependency edge between members goes to a lower layer or is a same-layer edge of docs/design/03 section 2; architecture.toml lists exactly those same-layer edges, the two ARCH-004 decoders and every crate of section 2 with its layer",
   "oracle": "the same-layer paragraph and the ARCH-004 row of docs/design/03 section 2, against Cargo's resolver graph"},
  {"id": "AC-3",
   "check": "cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace --locked && cargo deny check",
   "expect": "each command exits 0",
   "oracle": "rustfmt, clippy with the workspace lints of the root Cargo.toml, and cargo-deny against deny.toml and supply-chain/licences.toml"},
  {"id": "AC-4",
   "check": "gh run list --workflow verify.yml --event workflow_dispatch --branch issue/2 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion --limit 5, then gh run view <databaseId> --json headSha,jobs for the run whose headSha equals git rev-parse origin/issue/2",
   "expect": "the jobs 'fmt, clippy and tests (ubuntu-26.04)', 'fmt, clippy and tests (macos-26)', 'fmt, clippy and tests (windows-2025)' and 'cargo-deny' have conclusion success on that headSha",
   "oracle": "verify.yml on GitHub's hosted runners, run by workflow_dispatch on the head commit of issue/2 (#454; the session triggers it with gh workflow run verify.yml --ref issue/2)"},
  {"id": "AC-5",
   "check": "cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p grdr-proto -p grdr-schema -p grdr-model -p grdr-core -p grdr-llm-proto -p grdr-fastpath -p grdr-wasm",
   "expect": "exit 0",
   "oracle": "rustc for the wasm32-unknown-unknown target pinned in rust-toolchain.toml (ARCH-003)"},
  {"id": "AC-6",
   "check": "git ls-files crates/*/AGENTS.md programs/*/AGENTS.md bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/AGENTS.md",
   "expect": "22 paths, one per crate of R1 and R2, each containing every heading of docs/agents/templates/crate-AGENTS.md, with a header whose layer, privilege, surface, squad and trust core equal its row of R3's table",
   "oracle": "the template's headings and header fields, and R3's table"},
  {"id": "AC-7",
   "check": "cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 --no-deps --manifest-path bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/Cargo.toml && cargo fmt --manifest-path bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/Cargo.toml -- --check && cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings && git grep -n -F '// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause' -- bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/src/lib.rs && git grep -n -F '#![no_std]' -- bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/src/lib.rs",
   "expect": "each command exits 0; in the metadata the package's license is GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause, its dependencies list is empty and metadata.grdr equals its row of R3's table; the SPDX match is line 1; the root workspace's cargo metadata (AC-1) does not list the package as a member",
   "oracle": "ADR-0004 for the licence and SPDX line, design/10 R2 for no dependencies, and rustfmt and clippy with the crate's own copy of the root workspace lints (R10)"},
  {"id": "AC-8",
   "check": "git ls-files crates/grdr-proto/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-schema/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-model/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-core/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-llm-proto/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-fastpath/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-ffi/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-wasm/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-fastpath-ffi/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-ports/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-ports-testkit/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-crypto/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-wire/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-sensor-linux/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-store-local/src/lib.rs crates/grdr-sandbox-engine/src/lib.rs programs/grdr-daemon/src/main.rs bpf/grdr-sensor-linux-bpf/src/lib.rs, then git grep -L -F '#![deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects)]' -- the same 18 paths",
   "expect": "git ls-files prints all 18 paths; git grep -L prints no path",
   "oracle": "R4's list, which follows the layer rule of ADR-0022 and the privileged rows of R3's table"}
]}
```

### Risk tier
high (trust-core paths: architecture.toml and Cargo.lock as gate configuration under D-63, and bpf/**, programs/grdr-daemon/**, crates/grdr-sandbox-engine/**, crates/grdr-crypto/**, crates/grdr-fastpath/**, crates/grdr-ffi/**, crates/grdr-fastpath-ffi/** and crates/grdr-core/src/policy.rs in security/trust-core.paths). eval-security, eval-adversarial and two passing evaluators on different models judge it (owner instruction 7). An empty skeleton has no behaviour, so no reference model or soak applies; AC-4's three-system run is its matrix evidence.

### Trust core
yes
